title: The Joseon Dynasty Built an Entire Planned City Inside These Walls
mediaSource: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress planned city Jeongjo walls 5.74 km UNESCO

scenes.title: Joseon did not just build a fortress here
scenes.narration: Hwaseong Fortress was part of King Jeongjo's larger plan to establish a new urban and political center in Suwon.

scenes.title: The walls stretch about 5.74 kilometers
scenes.narration: According to UNESCO, Hwaseong's walls extend roughly 5.74 kilometers and surround the historic center of Suwon.

scenes.title: Its design blended different military ideas
scenes.narration: The fortress combined traditional Korean construction with military concepts and technologies circulating across East Asia and beyond.

scenes.title: A royal palace stood inside
scenes.narration: Hwaseong Haenggung served as a temporary royal palace when King Jeongjo visited Suwon and became a key center for royal events.

scenes.title: The old walls still meet the modern city
scenes.narration: Today neighborhoods, shops, and homes sit directly beside the fortress, placing eighteenth-century architecture inside everyday urban life.

scenes.title: A 200-year-old planned city still shapes Suwon
scenes.narration: Hwaseong is more than preserved stone walls. It remains part of the living structure and identity of modern Suwon.
